seo_title: Import Kurtis from India to Canada Wholesale: Duty, GST & Labels
seo_description: Guide for Canadian boutiques importing Indian kurtis: 18% duty, GST/HST, Business Number, CARM, bilingual fibre labels and CA number, plus MOQ 15–20 pieces from Jaipur.
body:
## Quick answer

Indian women's garments entering Canada usually pay **18% customs duty** plus **GST (5%)** and any **provincial tax** (HST or PST). You need a **CRA Business Number with an import account** and to be registered in **CARM**. Labels must show **fibre content in English and French** and a **CA dealer identification number**.

## Duty and tax at a glance

| Item | Rule |
|---|---|
| Customs duty (MFN) | 18% (confirm your exact tariff line) |
| GST | 5% |
| Provincial tax | HST or PST depending on province |
| Low-value threshold for non-US/Mexico shipments | Only C$20, so almost all shipments pay tax |
| Typical express transit from India | About 4–6 days |

## Documents you need

- **Commercial invoice** from the supplier
- **IEC** on the Indian side – we have this
- Your **Business Number** with an import (RM) account
- **CARM** registration

## Labelling

Under the Textile Labelling Act, garments need **fibre content in both English and French** and a **CA identification number** (or your name and address). We can stitch labels to these requirements.

## Tips for boutiques

- Include duty and GST in your landed cost from the start
- Diwali, Vaisakhi and the summer wedding season are peak times
- Larger, less frequent shipments reduce clearance costs
